All of the details are there, but it's only organized about 70% to 85% of the way. I'm posting this both to help players play the game better but to also receive input on improvements to the game.

Feel free to browse and comment. Thanks!
Dungeon Raiders 2 - The entirety of my design document

I fleshed out most of the areas and added a few more graphics. I feel like I'm 90%-95% done. I'm hoping to add more reasons behind some of the formulas and algorithms.

I recommend starting at the beginning and reading the "High-Level Game Flow" (it's 7 bullets). From there you can skip around to whatever interests you.

My original design document was just a long bulleted list in OneNote. I coded by turning the bullets into even more bullets of smaller tasks (a few at a time of course). For this design document I walked through the code by hand and converted it back into a design document. This turned out to be a great exercise as I found 1 minor bug, 2 minor display issues, and came up with a new adventure idea.

My new adventure idea is the "Spider Killer Adventure". If you encounter one of these rooms, you acquire a one-time method of killing the spider. If you are quite lucky, you'll encounter all 3 Spider Killer Adventures in a dungeon with only 4 Warning Types... you'll make a fortune in gems!

I'm using Unity's Analytics to measure how long people play. My goal, my definition of success, is that the game gets more play than the time I spent creating it. I've currently invested 170 hours into this game (and a small amount of cash). The game has currently been played 17 hours 58 minutes. (Genuine) Yippee! Thanks to all of you who played!
